description: REQ-509's own Acceptance Criteria (behavioral-spec.md) requires: 'An integration-style test using real (unmodified) guard modules with a fixture forcing a guard-block on the first-picked slot asserts the reroute picks a different slot AND the guard-blocked slot's own skip record is preserved verbatim in the ledger (not overwritten/silenced).' The implementing test, PROP-509b (always-act-reroute.test.mjs:550-576), asserts the first half (different slot picked) unconditionally, but wraps the SECOND half -- the actual 'verbatim ledger preservation' claim REQ-509's edge case exists to guarantee -- inside `if (skillErrorOrWakeForFirstPick) { assert.ok(...) }`, where `skillErrorOrWakeForFirstPick = allLines.find((l) => l.slot === 'earn/sol-trade')`. Tracing runAlwaysActWake's REQ-506 reroute branch (index.mjs:774-800) shows it NEVER writes any ledger.jsonl line for the just-picked, rerouted-away-from slot -- the branch only mutates `attemptsUsed`/`currentOfferedSlots` and `continue`s to the next attempt; the ONLY ledger writes in this function happen at a terminal escalation or the final successful pick. Separately, `classifyLayer({kind:'wake'})` (harness-health.mjs) returns 'clean' for this guard-blocked-but-exit-0 outcome, so `appendHarnessFailure` is also never invoked (index.mjs:765-772's `if (failureLayer !== 'clean')` guard is false). Consequently `skillErrorOrWakeForFirstPick` is PROVABLY undefined on every run of this test -- the `if` block is dead code, the assertion it guards NEVER executes, and the test passes regardless of whether the guard's skip record is actually preserved anywhere. Ground truth: it is NOT preserved anywhere -- no file (ledger.jsonl or harness-failures.jsonl) records the guard-blocked slot's own skip reason for this wake. This is both a test_quality defect (a money-safety-critical AC's only verification is unreachable) and a requirement_mismatch (REQ-509's own stated AC is not actually satisfied by the implementation): an operator inspecting the ledger after a real guard-block-then-reroute event has no record of which slot was blocked or why, only the final rerouted pick.

additionalEvidence.snippet: if (kind === 'wake' && isEarnActionSlot(slot) && noRealizedAction(earnLine)) { ... attemptsUsed = state.attemptsUsedNext; currentOfferedSlots = rerouteTargets; reinforcement = null; continue; } -- no ledger write for the just-rerouted-away-from slot anywhere in this branch.

export function classifyLayer(record) { const kind = record && record.kind; if (CLEAN_KINDS.has(kind)) return 'clean'; ... } -- kind:'wake' (the guard-blocked-but-exit-0 outcome) classifies as 'clean', so appendHarnessFailure (index.mjs:765-772) is also never invoked for this attempt.

An integration-style test using real (unmodified) guard modules with a fixture forcing a guard-block on the first-picked slot asserts the reroute picks a different slot and the guard-blocked slot's own skip record is preserved verbatim in the ledger (not overwritten/silenced).
